Q: How to properly unit test a .NET project with multiple target frameworks, given implementation differences among targets? A:

The multiple test project approach can still work decently by putting actual tests in a Shared Files project.

Once created, simply add it as a project reference to your various tests projects and any files will be automatically included in the build without needing to reference each file individually.

When it comes to API availability, the shared files can make use of preprocessor directives such as #if NET_5_0_OR_GREATER to conditionally compile, just like projects making use of multi-targetting.

A big advantage of this approach over a single multi-targetting test project is the IDE will treat each target as being distinct, will full support for the VS Test Explorer for instance.

If using MSTest, you can also enhance your filtering options by marking your test classes with the TestCategory attribute, providing it with a conditionally compiled string constant. This will generate an additional filter for your tests based on the target framework. You can likely find equivalents in other testing frameworks.

Q: Why do I still get this error: useSearchParams() should be wrapped in a suspense boundary at page "/404" A:

if you are using next js 16, make shure you removed --turbopack flag in package.json.
Turbopack is now the default bundler in Next.js.

Q: Import of xml libraries in java17 A:

Probably an IDE config issue, not a missing library.

Your IDE probably doesn't recognize that you're using Java 17, or the project isn't set up correctly

  • (if on eclipse) Make sure you see "JRE System Library [JavaSE-17] in your Libraries tab. If it says Java 1.8, click "Edit" and change to Java 17.

  • (if on IntelliJ IDEA) Set "Project SDK" to your JDK 17 and then set "Project language level" to "17".

  • (if on VScode) Check java.configuration.runtimes in settings and then make sure your it points to JDK 17.

the imports should work immediately as they are part of the standard library
